question: Find the median of the data 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **data** in ascending order: 11, 15, 16, 17, **19**, **21**, 33, 51, 71, 75.

Since the total number of terms (n = 10) is **even**, the median is the **average** of the two middle terms.

Middle terms are the 5th (19) and 6th (21) values.

Median = (19 + 21) ÷ 2 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:** 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17

**Formula Used:**

If n is **even**, Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02d428aa922d857b7ae4c5b37a2a530645320c7de270926cf69869d5a8401b40.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Arrange data in ascending order: 11, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 33, 51, 71, 75

⇒ Step 2: Number of observations (n) = 10

⇒ Step 3: Median = [(10/2)th term + (10/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 4: Median = [5th term + 6th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 5: Median = [19 + 21] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 6: Median = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd Observations

If n is odd, the median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation after arranging the data in order.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).</p
